scene sky
It’s a perfectly normal morning.

But it isn’t perfectly normal for long as the first thing I see when I step outside (Apart from an obnoxiously blue sky) is a name on my caller ID I am not yet prepared to deal with this early in the morning.
And yet I tap on the answer button as my breakfast today was small and gorging myself on attention might assist in making up for that.
: Good morning, Nodoka.
: And good morning to you as well, Father.
: I am not your father.
: But wouldn’t it be great if you were?
: Not really, no. One semi-daughter is enough for me. And I'm sure Ami is a much better cook than you anyway.
: Unfortunate. But tell me, do you have anything planned for the rest of the day? And perhaps tomorrow as well?
: Am I being invited to something?
: You are. And I solemnly swear it will not be a locker room this time.
: Is this another set-up?
: Why, yes. But it’s also not what you’re thinking.

: You see, I’ve decided to play matchmaker this morning and set up my roommate with Rin as it has been far too long without the two of them engaging in coitus and the lesbian energy is burning a hole in my brain.
: And, this may come as a surprise to you, but I just so happen to need my brain for brain stuff.
: You realize you aren’t exactly playing “matchmaker” if the two of them are already together, right?
: I suppose. But I’ll take it as a win so long as one of the two winds up with a tongue inside of them tonight. And no, I am not referring to the one that already lives inside of their mouths.
: Weird. But why do you need me?
: So I don’t wind up as a third wheel of course.
: Additionally, there’s a bit of a detour we need to take on the way to hopeful lesbian intercourse and it’s one I’d thoroughly enjoy having you there for.
: How quickly can you make it to the station near our school?
: I haven’t even said yes yet.
: Then I will say it for you. Yes. Now, how quickly can you make it to the station near our school?
: Nodoka-
: Excellent. We’ll wait there, then.
: I look forward to seeing you, Sensei.
: Just as you should look forward to what you will see.
scene black
Nodoka hangs up the phone and...it looks like I don’t have much of a say in what I’m going to do today.
As I make my way to the station, I wonder what sort of push is necessary to get Rin and Otoha to finally take the next step in their relationship.
There’s a tinge of jealousy of course as I, regretfully, won’t be involved. But more than anything, there’s an overflowing curiosity of what Nodoka plans to do in order to enable this.
Being a male, I’m obviously no expert when it comes to lesbian relationships, but I’m pretty sure most of them don’t require a team of onlookers in order to kick off.
There’s really no point in thinking about any of this. These are all just thoughts I use to occupy the blank space in time between places A and B.
Not just because the world will move regardless of whether or not I want it to-
But because Nodoka is always so many steps ahead of me that I can never figure out what she’s plotting to begin with.
scene nodokatrain1
Upon arriving at the station, I am greeted by two surprised expressions and one oozing a disturbing sense of both pride and accomplishment.
: Sensei? What are you doing here?
: Good question, Otoha. Ask your roommate.
scene nodokatrain2
: Nodoka, what-
: I invited him, of course. Three is such an odd number, don’t you think? And quite literally at that.
: Four is much more balanced. Plus it prevents me from becoming a third wheel.
: How would you be the third wheel when you’re the one who invited us? Otoha and I are only coming along because we want to support you.
: Support her in what? I still don’t know what we’re doing.
scene nodokatrain3
: Nodoka’s new book just came out a week ago and she’s doing a signing downtown today.
: Neither one of us have read it, but we were promised free food and didn’t have anything else to do, so...yeah.
: So I take it this “detour” she mentioned on the phone is the main event after all?
: Well, excuse me for being humble. You wouldn’t have come along if I’d done nothing but toot my own horn over the phone and, as my surrogate father, I wanted you to be here for this.
: I think you’ll come to be quite proud of me by the end of the day, Sensei.
: So, the goal was to make me proud and not that other thing you said on the phone?
scene nodokatrain4
: Can it not be both?
: I’m confused. What did you tell Sensei on the phone?
: It’s probably best for everyone if we didn’t talk about that.
: Welp, that about answers that question. I suddenly know where this is going.
: I just kind of figured with today being, you know, an actual big event for you that you had a different motivation in mind this time.
scene nodokatrain5
: Am I seriously the only person who doesn’t know what’s going on right now?
: It doesn’t matter at the end of the day. We already signed up for this and I’d feel weird backing down on supporting Nodoka just because she is once again thinking...Nodoka things.
: We’re still getting free food, though...right? Because if that was a lie, I’m going to punch someone. And process of elimination says that person would have to be Sensei.
: How? Why? No.
: Don’t even worry about it, Rin. Look at it this way — Sensei being here means that the two of us can hang out more and that the two of them can keep having their weird...father-daughter thing.
: Why is everyone so set on making me Nodoka’s dad?
: Don’t I look cute in this suit, Papa? Don’t you want to just tear it off and play with me before Mommy comes home?
: Yes, but that is beside the point.
scene nodokatrain6
: It doesn’t have to be...
: And on that note, I’m walking over to the platform. Rin, if you’d be so kind as to accompany me?
: Sorry, Sensei...Duty calls. Enjoy your daughter, though.
scene nodokatrain7
: Shall we head out as well? Or do you want to wait for the next train and give the two of them some breathing room?
: Don’t you have a book signing to get to? I figured you’d be in a rush.
: It’s my signing. It’s not as if they can do it without me. Besides, I have plenty of readers who’d sit there for days while waiting for me. I’m kind of a big deal.
scene nodokatrain8
: Look- I’ve got a purse and everything. There isn’t even anything in it. I am literally only carrying this because it makes me look the part.
: Nodoka, be honest. Why did you want me here for this? You’ve never shown me any of your writing before. Why do you just now want me to be “proud” of you? That can’t be it, right?
scene nodokatrain9
: Maybe I’ve fallen for you?
: Are you even capable of that?
: Who knows? Maybe we’ll find out today.
: Nodoka-
: A good author won’t just explain the plot, Sensei. A good author lets the reader find out on their own.
: If you want to know what it is I want...or what I’m hoping to gain by dragging you along with me, why not just spend a little more time reading?
: You might like what you find.
: You and these damn book metaphors.
: The train is here. Are we leaving or not?
scene black
: Fine, come on. But I can’t guarantee I’ll like whatever it is you’re trying to get me to read.
: You don’t have to like it.
: You don’t even have to get it.
: You just have to be there.
scene nodokatrain10
Despite being pressed for time, Nodoka takes it upon herself to grab a quick cup of coffee from a kiosk near the platform and the two of us just barely make it onto the train before it departs.
Thankfully, there’s enough room for us to grab seats almost directly across from Rin and Otoha, but neither one of us pay them any mind as we don’t want to interrupt anything.
Even if the “detour” I was advised of is today’s primary objective, it would still be nice if we’d be able to force the two of them a little bit closer together.
I say we as if I play any part in this when, in all actuality, I know I’m only here to keep Nodoka entertained.
But, I suppose that goes both ways.
Because even if she occasionally does things that shock and appall me, I’m no different.
If anything, I’m worse.
She knows this.
She knows this, yet she still smiles at me like that.
: Would you like a sip of my coffee, Sensei? Act now and you’ll be able to steal a bit of my saliva before it dries up.
: I’m good. There are better and less caffeinated ways to obtain your saliva if I really want to.
: Do you think you’ve saved up enough points for that?
: Depends. How many do I get for joining you today?
scene nodokatrain11
: I wonder. It’s been so long since I awarded any that I’m not quite sure what their value is anymore.
scene nodokatrain12
: Let’s just say you’ve earned enough for either a kiss or some light groping and we can call it a day?
: Is that redeemable on the train?
: It’s redeemable anywhere you please. Though, I can’t guarantee your reward won’t be cut short by angry passengers if you make a redemption right now.
: I’ll hang on to this intangible coupon for the time being then. I’m looking forward to finding out that it expires roughly thirty seconds from now.
scene nodokatrain13
: Unfortunately, it expired in the middle of that sentence. Too bad. And here I was starting to get a little turned on.
: So, this book you just released-
: Changing the subject as soon as I admit my arousal? How rude.
: You’re always aroused. I’ll have plenty of more opportunities to ask about that in the future.
scene nodokatrain14
: You’ve had plenty of time to ask about my writing as well. And yet, here we are — violently penetrating a series of underground tunnels until we’re spewed out on the other side.
: Leave it to you to sexualize trains, I guess.
: Anything can be sexualized if one tries hard enough. And any hole can be penetrated with enough persistence and force. Which isn’t to say one should penetrate all holes, but-
: Tell me more about your writing. What’s this book about?
scene nodokatrain15
: That’s a good question. What is this book about?
: I feel like that’s something you should probably know as the author.
: By conventional means, sure. But when one literary work contains so many different ideas, it’s near impossible to simply explain what it’s about, isn’t it? It’s something that must be experienced.
: That is probably one of the most pretentious things I’ve ever heard.
scene nodokatrain16
: Let’s just say it’s about the folly of man. Or the pleasures in struggling.
: Sounds boring.
: You don’t read much anymore, do you?
: I don’t read at all. Though, I can’t quite remember when I ever did in the first place.
: I imagine you stopped around the same time you stopped writing. To which I’d say, “how sad.”

: There’s a great deal you’re missing out on by living the life you lead, Sensei. But, at the same time, I know there must be plenty you experience that you’d never be able to pull from the pages of a book.
: Perhaps learning about my latest work will be the call to action you need to get back into the literary world? It’d be wonderful to have a partner there, you know.
: Is Futaba not enough of a partner for you?
: Futaba is a darling and I would kill for her. But we both know she’s nowhere remotely close to the level we are.
: How do you even know my level? You’ve never read anything I’ve written. In fact, I don't think I’ve ever read anything I’ve written.
: Hmm...intuition, perhaps?
: Or maybe I’m secretly a beloved fan of yours who’s been following you ever since I was a little girl? Desperately awaiting the day her favorite writer returns to the game?
: That would...actually explain a lot. But I doubt that’s the case.
scene nodokatrain17
: It would have been interesting if it were, though.
: Unfortunately, life is far too mundane to be filled with fun coincidences like that.
: Is that why you got into writing in the first place? You were too...bored with life or whatever?
: Mmm...no. No, I don’t believe that’s what it was.
: While it may be true that my days lack in color, they’ve always made up for that in...hmm...how should I put this?
scene nodokatrain18
: Incontrovertible peculiarity?
: I’m going to need you to elaborate.
scene nodokatrain19
: Let’s just say I’ve lived a life that not many would understand...
: And that the reason I’m so obsessed with books is that there was someone before me who may have inadvertently caused me to...inherit that interest.
: I’m going to need you to continue to elaborate.
: Would you believe me if I told you I came from nothing?
: As in...you were poor?
: Perhaps it’s better if I don’t attempt to explain things at all. It’ll only make me appear insane.
: Nodoka, essentially everything you do makes you appear insane. An explanation of your childhood won’t tip the scales.
scene nodokatrain20
: Then why don’t you go ahead and picture younger Nodoka as a little amoeba — feasting on tiny aquatic plants to keep herself sustained and protected from the big, scary world?
: Or a cute little tardigrade — clinging to a patch of grease in your kitchen sink that you’ve neglected to clean over the past several weeks?
: I’m going to picture you as neither of those things because you are a human being.
: That I am. And an interesting one at that.
: But before I was human, I hadn’t even been a thought.
: To this day, I am not a thought. I am a girl who simply is. And I will continue to be because I can’t not. Do you understand?
: No.
scene nodokatrain21
: Exactly.
: There are things in this world that are beyond comprehension.
: But what if I told you there was another one outside of it?
: Another...what? Another world?
: An infinite amount of them. Each one remarkably different from the next. And that some things are only impossible to comprehend because we’re not meant to comprehend them.
: What if we’re meant to be somewhere else?
: What if this world is just a mistake?
: Then...we live with it, I guess. There’s not really anything else we can do, is there?
scene nodokatrain22
: But what if there is?
: What if we can go somewhere else?

: What if someone has been somewhere else but everyone thinks they’re crazy and no one believes them because the idea of another world layered on top of this one is absurd? It’s insane. It’s impossible.
: If we found it, would they believe us then?
: If we could replicate or emulate or simulate another world, would they believe us then?
: Or would we be forced to suffer in silence because it’s all too incomprehensible? What happens if we find it? What happens if we go there? How do we get there?
: How.
: Do.
: We.
: Get.
: There?
scene nodokatrain23
: So yeah. That’s basically why I started writing.
: That...
: That didn’t tell me anything at all.
scene nodokatrain24
: Sure it did.
: You’re just not meant to get it yet.
scene black
: It seems to me like that was just an overly-convoluted way to dodge the question. But hey, if you don’t want me to know, that’s fine. I like keeping my affairs private too.
: That’s just the thing, Sensei...I do want you to know.
: It’s just impossible to believe as none of it is based in logic. It’s just something that is because it is.
: It’s a feeling.
: But it’s a feeling that moves me.
: It’s the only thing that moves me.
: And that’s exactly why I need to figure out how to make you understand.
: I need to figure out how to make all of you understand.
: If I can’t, my existence means nothing.
: And I will return to what I was in the beginning.
: I won’t even be a thought.
I lean back in my seat and let the rest of the ride go by in silence — but it’s not because I’m confused or shocked.
It’s because, for some reason beyond my comprehension as well-
I believe her.
I wish I could tell you why.
